prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Generate exactly ONE isolated reusable building sprite for tianshu default building-map, Ming dynasty northern Chinese prefectural city (Beijing/Datong/Xian regional vocabulary), anonymous original period-inspired design, not a measured heritage reconstruction. Input image is STYLE reference only: match its restrained realistic material detail, fine grey clay roof tiles, weathered masonry and natural matte wood, and same detail density. Change architecture to Ming north as specified. Orthographic 2:1 dimetric ground projection, camera yaw45 elevation30, east axis down-right slope +0.5 and north up-right slope -0.5; parallel ground edges, vertical posts, no perspective convergence. South entrance on screen lower-left edge. Complete building on thin rectangular ground-contact footprint with readable left, front, right corners, footprint axis ratio as specified, no thick pedestal, no soil island. Neutral soft light from SCREEN UPPER LEFT, short soft contact shadow only toward lower-right. TRUE transparent RGBA background and generous blank alpha0 margins all four sides; no skyline, no surrounding scenery. No people, writing, Chinese pseudo-glyphs, text, plaques, signs, banners, watermark, grid, modern fittings, plastic render, cartoon, ink wash, oversaturation, dense lanterns, white halo or baked checkerboard. Only building and its own footprint; include all eaves and base corners uncropped. Asset ID bld_kit_ming_north_wangfu. Footprint 22 metres east-west by 18 metres north-south. A princely residence ceremonial module, one single-eaved hip-and-gable principal hall, two subordinate hard-gabled wings and a modest southern gate around a large rectangular axial courtyard. Dark green glazed tiles only on main hall, grey clay tiles on wings, muted cinnabar posts, grey brick/red-ochre plaster enclosing walls, limited desaturated blue-green beam pattern, no gold mass, no bright yellow imperial roofing, no extravagant double-eave Forbidden City copy. Thin stone foundations. Principal hall ROOF is distinctly HIP-AND-GABLE, not the reference's gabled roof. Side wing roofs proper YINGSHAN hard-gabled, masonry flush gable ends. Exact ground axes rise/run 1:2; no steep 30 degree ground diagonals.
